paragraphs.text: Ichthyosis with erythrokeratoderma is an autosomal dominant disorder of cornification. It begins early and presents as ichthyosiform erythroderma or erythrokeratoderma, with a thickened, dense stratum corneum that reflects abnormal desquamation (Gong et al., 2023). Takeichi et al. (2023) described large hyperkeratotic pigmented plaques on the trunk as a characteristic finding.

paragraphs.text: Gong et al. (2023) performed whole-exome sequencing in 3 families with early-onset ichthyosiform erythroderma or erythrokeratoderma: 1 familial case and 2 sporadic cases. They identified 2 heterozygous variants affecting gly50 in the KLK11 gene, one of which was a c.149G-A transition resulting in a gly50-to-glu (G50E) substitution. Both variants lie around the signal peptide cleavage site. The available evidence does not specify which patients carried which variant. In overexpression systems, the variants perturbed signal peptide cleavage. The G50E variant was mislocalized within the cell, and its extracellular secretion was impaired. The patients' stratum corneum showed significantly decreased trypsin-like and chymotrypsin-like proteolytic activity.

(2023) found that the KLK11 variants perturbed signal peptide cleavage in overexpression systems, which led to subcellular mislocalization and impaired extracellular secretion of the G50E variant. The patients' stratum corneum showed significantly reduced trypsin-like and chymotrypsin-like proteolytic activity. It also showed reduced proteolysis of desmoglein-1 and delayed degeneration of corneodesmosomes, indicating delayed desquamation.

paragraphs.text: Gong et al. (2023) used whole-exome sequencing to study 3 families with early-onset ichthyosiform erythroderma or erythrokeratoderma: 1 familial case and 2 sporadic cases. They identified a heterozygous c.149G-A transition in the KLK11 gene, resulting in a gly50-to-glu (G50E) substitution near the signal peptide cleavage site. This was one of 2 heterozygous KLK11 variants affecting gly50 found in these families. The evidence does not specify which patients carried this particular variant. In overexpression systems, the G50E variant perturbed signal peptide cleavage, was mislocalized within the cell, and showed impaired extracellular secretion. Mice homozygous for the equivalent Klk11 variant (G44E) had hyperkeratosis and abnormal desquamation.
